Definition: from G1223 and G2224; to gird tightly:--gird.
BiblicalUsage: To gird oneself is to tie up the loose robe for work, and John uses it three times for Jesus and Peter. Jesus girds Himself with a towel to wash the disciples' feet, and Peter girds his fisher's coat to swim to the risen Lord.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the girding in John is the picture of a servant's love. Jesus tied on the towel before He took the basin, and Peter tied on his coat before he swam to shore, and both were hurrying to the Lord they loved.
